newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burma denies sheltering wanted drug suspect.
newsitem.headline: Burma denies sheltering wanted drug suspect.

text.p: Burma's military government has dismissed reports that it was sheltering a man accused of masterminding the biggest heroin haul in United States history.
A government statement received by Reuters on Thursday said reports that drug suspect Li Yung Chung had settled in Burma after jumping bail in Thailand were unfounded.
"Myanmar (Burma) has nothing to do with this mess, but again, very conveniently and automatically Myanmar becomes a scapegoat when there seems to be a problem in the world," the statement said.

The statement referred to a report in the Bangkok Post newspaper that Li, also known by a Thai name Phongsak Rogjanasakul, had settled in Rangoon after jumping bail in Thailand while awaiting extradition to the United States.

Li is the main suspect in a drug haul worth up to $122 million and is wanted in the United States. Thai authorities have said they believe he fled to Burma shortly after being granted bail by a Thai judge in early February.
Reports that Li had fled the country surfaced in early March when he failed to show up at court.
The United States has complained about the Thai court decision to grant bail to Li, who has a Thai identity card, but is also said to have links to Burma.

Opium warlord Khun Sa, also wanted on drugs charges in the United States, is living in Rangoon after surrendering to Burmese troops last year. Burma has vowed not to extradite him and said the government would deal with him in its own way.

Li was indicted by a New York court in May 1996 in connection with the largest heroin haul ever in the United States -- the seizure in 1991 of 486 kg (nearly 1,070 lb) of the drug in Hayward, California.
Drug officials put the U.S. street value between $180,000 to $250,000 per kg, making the haul worth $87.5 million to $122 million.
